target.title: fix(mcp): suppress unhandled error on stderr pipe in stdio transport
target.body:
## Summary

Add a noop error listener on `child.stderr` before piping it to `stderrStream` in the MCP stdio transport, matching the existing error handlers on `child.stdin` (line 82) and `child.stdout` (line 87).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `child.stderr.pipe(this.stderrStream)` is called without an error handler on the source stream. If stderr emits an error (EPIPE, I/O failure), the pipe propagates it as an unhandled `error` event, crashing the process. Stdin and stdout already have error handlers; stderr was the only one missing.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw main

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

The new test "suppresses stderr pipe errors" creates a transport with `stderr: "pipe"`, starts it, then emits an error on `child.stderr`. The `expect(...).not.toThrow()` assertion proves the noop handler suppresses the error.

**Before-fix evidence**: `child.stderr.pipe(this.stderrStream)` was called without `child.stderr.on("error", ...)`. Node PassThrough streams throw on `emit("error")` when no error listener is registered.

**Observed result after fix**: Stderr pipe errors are silently suppressed. The existing behavior for stdin and stdout errors is preserved.

**What was not tested**: Live EPIPE on a real MCP child process stderr pipe. The test directly emits an error on the PassThrough stream.

## Risk

Low. One-line addition. Matches the existing pattern on lines 82 and 87 of the same file.
